classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the triangle's perpendicular height from the square, then subtract its area from the square's area.

content.prompt: A square of side length $8\text{ cm}$ has a triangle removed from it, as shown on the right. What is the remaining area?

spec.description: Square with its top edge labelled 8 cm. Segments join both top corners to an unlabelled point on the bottom edge, right of its midpoint. The central downward-pointing triangle retains meaningful blue shading; the outer regions are unfilled. The vertex position is schematic and supplies no additional measurement.
spec.mathematics: The central triangle has base 8 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm regardless of its bottom vertex's horizontal position.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and region shading are visible; no calculated areas are shown.

answer.worked:
Taking the shaded central triangle as the removed triangle, its base and perpendicular height are both $8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=8\times8\\A_{\text{square}}&=64\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times8\times8\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=32\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{remaining}}&=64-32\\A_{\text{remaining}}&=32\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
